learning_outcomes.text: Students can solve interdisciplinary and integrated closed technical problems and case studies in a methodical way.
Students can convert a realistic problem into a mathematical model.
Students can break down a problem into sub-problems.
Students can use their mathematical background to solve the various sub-problems.
Students can interpret the result of the calculations.
Using ICT tools for the engineer.
Students develop the following attitudes: meticulousness, a critical attitude, independence and sense of responsibility.

syllabus_topics: Converting technical-scientific problems into simpler sub-questions

Combining mathematical techniques from analysis (functions of one variable, graphs, integrals, derivatives), algebra (solving systems, algebraic calculations, polar coordinates, vector calculus), plane geometry, spatial geometry, trigonometry
Understanding mathematical models in relation to reality
Developing mathematical models into solutions for original problems
Simple matrix operations with geometric interpretation
Aspects of graphic modeling in a technical analysis and design process
Designing and building a physical object in a team
Supporting design with simple scientific experiments
Using skills learned in Mathematical modeling for problem solving
Applying basic knowledge from first semester technical-scientific courses: mathematics (analysis and algebra), chemistry, and mechanics

assessment_methods.method: Test on Mathematical basic techniques (multiple-choice and open questions)
Test on Mathematical modeling for problem solving (open questions)
Individual test on Graphic design (part of Designing in a team)
Team result for final product (design, report and presentation) (part of Designing in a team)
Daily work (part of Designing in a team)

assessment_rules: For each OLA, a separate score is determined. If the student passes 'Mathematical basic techniques' AND the scores for 'Mathematical modeling for problem solving' and 'Designing in a team' are both 8/20 or higher, the final result is the weighted average of these two OLAs. If the student fails 'Mathematical basic techniques' OR at least one of the scores for 'Mathematical modeling for problem solving' and 'Designing in a team' is less than 8/20, the final result is the weighted average of these two OLAs with a maximum of 7/20. Passed OLA results are transferred within the academic year. Resits for 'Mathematical basic techniques' and 'Mathematical modeling for problem solving' involve similar tests, while 'Designing in a team' offers a tailored re-examination.
